lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I'll let you get on.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: You! You're the one who opened that cage! I'd have rotted in there.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Odo Marrow, at your service. Peddler, tinker, very grateful man.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: My rescuer! Come, come, I kept the good things for you.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Can I see what you've got?

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Rings, gloves, boots. Half price for you. Well, nearly.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Who are you, if you don't mind me asking?

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Bandits took my cart and put me in a box. Very rude.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Now I sell from Sunford. It's safer here. Mostly.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Pleasure doing business, friend.

lines.speaker: freedPeddler
lines.text: Mind the bandits. They don't like to share.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Light be with you. You found me in the dark, and I won't forget it.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: I'm Aurelle. Sister Auriel taught me the light. Now I teach it here.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Welcome back. The sun is kind today.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Will you teach me?

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Open your hands. Let the light come through them, not from them.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a Lightbringer do?

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: We carry the dawn. Light to fight with, light to heal with.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Intelligence makes the light strong. Charisma makes it warm.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you think I'm ready for more?

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: You shine brighter than I do now. Take whatever you need.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: You're ready for the next lesson. Come, stand in the light.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Not yet. A clearer mind and a warmer heart first.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: I went to the Sunken Temple to pray. The naga had other plans.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Sunford is bright and quiet. I needed both.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Go gently. And let them see you coming.

lines.speaker: lightDisciple
lines.text: Walk in the light.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Haven't seen you before. You're the one who cleared the road?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Bram. I keep the forge. If you need a blade, come to me.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Heard the Goblin King's dead. Can't say I'll miss him.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Goblins trading in the square now. Never thought I'd see it.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: You let the Goblin King keep his crown. He'll be back, you know.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Whole realm's talking about you. Still need a whetstone, though?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Back again. What can I do for you?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Plain steel, fair prices. Have a look.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I've got some ore to sell.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Nuggets, eh? I'll take the lot. Fair weight, fair coin.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Could you teach me to smith?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Smithing? Hm. Hold the hammer like this, not like a club.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Strike when the metal glows brightest. Miss, and it's scrap. Go on.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I'd like to use your forge.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Forge is hot. Mind your fingers.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Bram. Thirty years at this anvil, give or take.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Horseshoes, ploughs, the odd sword. Lately, mostly swords.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What should I take with me out there?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: A shield, if you plan on getting hit. Most people do.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Heavy steel needs a strong arm. Work on your Strength first.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Heard anything lately?

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Bandits on the plains road. I'd start there, if I were you.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: The goblins come from the Hollows, past the plains. Their king's down there.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: East of the plains are the Whispering Woods. Folk say the trees move.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: There's smoke toward Oakhaven. An army's camped on the outskirts.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Ironhold steel's coming down the road again. Better than mine, if I'm honest.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Look after it and it'll look after you.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Not bad. Not good either. Keep at it.

lines.speaker: sunfordSmith
lines.text: Mind how you go.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Oh, hello! Are you buying, or just looking? Both are fine.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: I'm Tilly. Rings, charms, bits and pieces from all over.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Have you seen the goblin's stall? His prices are lower than mine. It's not fair.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: There you are! I put a few things aside I think you'll like.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Have a look. That one's lucky. Probably.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: I walk the roads and buy what people want to get rid of.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: And sometimes I find things. Bandits drop a lot when they run.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What are trinkets actually good for?

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: You can wear two, one on each hand. It all adds up out there.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Where did all this come from, really?

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Ah. You've got a way of asking, haven't you?

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Take this ring and let's not talk about where I found it.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: There's an old colosseum south of here. Shut tight while the goblins raid.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: The colosseum's open again. Eight waves, I hear. People bet on it.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Oakhaven pays well for anything shiny. It's east, past the woods.

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Come back when your purse is heavier!

lines.speaker: sunfordPeddler
lines.text: Safe travels. Hold on to your coin out there.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Stand up straight. You're speaking to a knight of the Iron Order.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Ser Aldric. I teach people to stand between others and harm.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Oakhaven still stands, and I hear you were on its wall. Well done.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: You opened Oakhaven's gate. I won't pretend I've forgotten. What do you want?

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: You killed the dragon on the peak? I'd have liked to see that.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: The Order thinks well of you. For its friends, my lessons cost less.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: The Order calls you an enemy. I'll still teach you. That's my choice, not theirs.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Back for more drills?

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Good. Watch closely, I'll only show you once.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does an Aegis Knight actually do?

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: We take the blows meant for others. It's simple, and it's hard.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: You'll need Strength for the shield and Endurance to keep it up.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: You're strong enough for most of what I know. Keep at your Endurance.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: You're ready for the next lesson. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Not yet. You'd tire before the shield did. More Strength, more Endurance.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about the Iron Order.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: We keep the roads safe and the law in hand. Some say too firmly.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Stand with us, and our armourers and teachers will remember you.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Practise until it's boring. Then keep going.

lines.speaker: trainerAegis
lines.text: Go carefully.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Oh, a student? Lovely. Maybe stand back a little.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: I'm Ember Wren. I teach fire. Mostly it does what I ask.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: You gave the core to the Circle! I can't wait to see what we learn from it.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: The Circle speaks highly of you. That means a discount, by the way.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: The Circle isn't happy with you. I'll still teach you, though. Quietly.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: You're back! Ready to light something?

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Right. Watch my hands, and keep your sleeves away from me.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a pyromancer do, exactly?

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Set things alight, mostly. Then make the fire spread where you want it.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: It all comes from Intelligence. The sharper the mind, the hotter the flame.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Honestly? You could teach some of this. Take whatever you like.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: You're ready for the next spell. Come on, I'll show you.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Not yet, I'm afraid. You need more Intelligence, or the fire takes over.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Who are the Circle of Aether?

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Scholars. We study what the world's made of. Some of it explodes.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Go and practise. Somewhere that won't catch, please.

lines.speaker: trainerPyro
lines.text: Take care of yourself!

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Didn't hear you come in. That's usually my trick.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Nettle Quickhand. I teach the quiet arts: daggers, shadows, leaving early.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Back again? Good. Nobody saw you, I hope.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Light feet, quick hands. Try not to trip over your own blade.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a shadow do?

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Strike where they aren't looking, then be somewhere else entirely.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: It all runs on Dexterity. Quick hands, quick feet, quick exits.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: You're quicker than me now. Take what you like, I won't even notice.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: You're ready for the next trick. Watch closely, I only do it once.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Not yet. Get quicker first, or the shadows trip you up.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Why teach here, in Sunford?

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Quiet town, honest folk. Nobody looks twice at a farmer's cloak. Perfect.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Off you go. Practise where the guards can't see.

lines.speaker: sfShadow
lines.text: Mind your purse.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Mind the rocks. Some of them are listening.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Harrow Flint. I teach the old earth magic: stone, roots, a little quake.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Ah, you're back. The ground told me you were coming.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Feet flat, breathe slow. Feel the weight under you. Good.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a geomancer do?

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Ask the earth for help. Walls when you need them, spikes when they don't.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Strength to hold the stone, Intelligence to shape it. You need both.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: The stone answers you before I do now. Take whatever you need.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: You're ready for the next lesson. Put your hand on the ground. Listen.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Not yet. More strength and a clearer head, or the stone won't listen.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Does the earth help the farms too?

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Every spring. The barley grows a hand taller and nobody knows why. Don't tell them.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Go on. And put that rock back where you found it.

lines.speaker: sfGeo
lines.text: Walk softly. The ground remembers.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: So you're the one from the road. Come here, let me look at you.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: I'm Mara. I've looked after this town for... oh, forty years now.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: The Hollows are quiet. It was a hard thing you did, but we sleep because of it.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Goblins selling things in my square. You talked them into that, didn't you?

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: You took his gold and left him his crown. I won't pretend I'm not disappointed.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Word came from Oakhaven. The gate held. I'm glad you were there.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Oakhaven burned, they say. I'd rather not hear how. Not today.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: They say you decided the fate of the Dread Fortress. From our little road to that.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Sit for a moment. The road will still be there.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I found a piece of an old map.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Captain Rook's map! He tore it up and hid the pieces before the goblins caught him.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Find all six and the X shows the way: somewhere in the Ashen Crags. Dig there, and the gold is yours.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Someone said you wanted to see me?

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: You held the road when our militia couldn't. The town put a little together.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: It isn't much. It's what we could spare.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What's troubling Sunford?

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: The raids come from the Goblin Hollows. They've crowned themselves a king.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: And you want him dead?

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: I want the raids to stop. How... well, that's for you to decide, down there.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: The Hollows are just past the plains. Please, be careful.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About the Goblin King...

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: He's gone, and the caravans run again. I won't ask how it felt.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: A trade pact. My mother would have fainted. Still, trade beats funerals.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Gold runs out quickly. Grudges don't. Remember that when the raids start.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about Sunford.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Farmers, mostly. A smith, a healer, two teachers who put up with us.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Rest here between journeys. That's what home is for.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Where should I go next?

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: The plains road, first. Without the caravans, we don't eat.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: The Goblin Hollows. Nothing else is safe while the raids go on.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: East, through the Whispering Woods. That's the road to Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Oakhaven is under siege. If the outskirts fall, the town goes with them.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: North, I think. The Ashen Crags, and Ironhold beyond. It only gets harder.

lines.speaker: elderMara
lines.text: Come back to us in one piece. That's all I ask.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Hold still a moment. No, you're fine. Habit, sorry.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: I'm Sister Lune. I patch up whatever the road breaks.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Still in one piece? Good. Sit down anyway.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Could you patch me up?

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Sit, rest a while. I'll fill your flasks before you go.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you have anything for mana?

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: This one's bitter. Drink it when your spells run dry.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How do the potions work?

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: You take a few flasks into every fight. Drink before you need to, not after.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: If you want to carry more, I can sell you a bigger belt.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: The goblins coat their sling stones in something. If you feel sick, come back.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: I've treated three spider bites from the Woods this week. Watch your step there.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Soldiers keep coming down from the north with burns. The Ashen Crags, they say.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Keep your belt full and your head down.

lines.speaker: sunfordHealer
lines.text: Look after yourself out there.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: You are the one who made the pact. My king says you are welcome here.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: I am Grik. I sell what goblins make. Good work, fair price.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: Friend. Good to see you again.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: Look, please. My family made these.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How is your king?

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: He eats well now. No more raids. My people are less hungry.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: He speaks of you often. With respect.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How do you like Sunford?

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: People still stare. But the baker gives me pie. I like the pie.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: My cousins dig in the black rock to the north. They say fire walks there now.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: Something is waking in the deep places. Goblins feel it in the ground.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: Thank you. Come again.

lines.speaker: goblinTrader
lines.text: Go safely, friend.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Psst. Got any junk in that bag? Old boots, bent swords? I'll play you for it.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Dob Tumbler. I play for fun, mostly. And for boots.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: You again! Got any more of that lovely junk?

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Deal me in.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Fee on the table. Lay your things down, highest price takes the point.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What are the rules?

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: We each lay an item. The pricier one wins the point. Two points wins the game.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Whatever you lay is mine, win or lose. Win three games in a row, though, and I've got something special.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Used to be a pedlar. Turns out people would rather bet their stuff than sell it.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you ever lose?

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: All the time! But I always go home with a new pair of boots.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Good game! That stuff of yours will look lovely on my shelf.

lines.speaker: sunfordGambler
lines.text: Bring more junk! Junk is my favourite.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: We'd be dead without you. Me and my boy both. Thank you.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Jory Toller. We farm outside the walls now. Well, we try.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: There's our hero. Come for a bite?

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Can I help with anything?

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Wolves out of the Whispering Woods keep taking our sheep.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Thin them out, would you? Eight should teach them.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About those wolves...

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: The wolves are still about. We heard them last night.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: The wolves won't trouble you again.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Quiet nights again. We can finally sleep.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Take this. It's not much, but it's honest.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Bandits took us from our field and left us in the woods to rot.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Oakhaven took us in. We pay it back in bread.

lines.speaker: freedFarmers
lines.text: Mind how you go.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: You got me out! I owe you everything. Well, a lot.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Kestrel Vane. Sefa Galewing taught me the bow. I can teach you what she taught me.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Hey! The wind's good today. Shall we practise?

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Feet apart. Breathe out. Let the wind carry it.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a Windrunner do?

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Run, shoot, run again. Never be where they aim.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Dexterity for quick feet. Skill, so every arrow lands.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: You're faster than me now. Take what you like.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: You're ready for the next one. Watch closely.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Not yet. Get quicker first, then come back.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: I was on my way to Silverbridge when the crags caught me.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Tell Sefa I'm alive, would you? She worries.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Go and practise. Somewhere windy.

lines.speaker: windDisciple
lines.text: Keep your eyes on the wind.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Another sword. Good. We need every one we can get.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Captain Hale. I command what's left of Oakhaven's watch.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: The gate held. Three hundred years, and one more. I owe you for that.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: You decided the Dread Fortress, they say. My walls feel small next to that.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Walls are still standing. For today, anyway.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Good to see you. Oakhaven hasn't forgotten.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How bad is it?

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Bad. A warlord called Krag has us surrounded, and he doesn't fight for free.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Who's paying him?

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: The Ashen Syndicate. They want a town of their own, and ours has walls.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Break his camp on the Oakhaven Outskirts. That's where this ends, one way or another.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About the siege...

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: They offered you a third of the town, didn't they? They offered me a quarter.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: The Syndicate will be after you now. Watch your back on the roads.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: A trade town. Anything going between the plains and the mountains pays a toll here.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: That's why everyone wants it. And why I won't give it up.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you answer to the Iron Order?

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: I answer to Oakhaven. The Order and I agree most days. Not every day.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: North of the woods the ground's black and burning. The Ashen Crags. Cultists, mostly.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Ironhold's stopped sending steel. Something's wrong in their mines.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: The far north's gone quiet. In my experience, that's never good.

lines.speaker: captainHale
lines.text: Keep your sword close.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: If you're after a helmet, I'm sorry. They're all up on the wall.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Odo. I make armour. Haven't slept much lately.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Still here. Still short of nearly everything.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Half my stock went to the wall. Take what's left, if it fits.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Raw ore! The armoury never has enough. Here's your pay.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: You want to learn the trade? Good. Oakhaven needs every hammer.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Watch the glow. Strike at its heart, three times, and the metal remembers.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: The anvil's yours. Make something that holds.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: I've armoured this town for twenty years. Never seen all of it worn at once.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What sort of armour should I wear?

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Plate, if you stand your ground. Leather, if you keep moving. Robes, if you're quick.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: If the siege breaks, I'll open the back room. The good plate's in there.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: It'll hold. It's held so far.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Good steel. The walls thank you.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Keep your head down out there.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: There you are! Come in. The back room's open, and it's open for you.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Master Odo, they call me now. Funny what a little peace does for business.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: From our gate to the Dread Fortress. I tell everyone I fitted your armour.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Good to see you. What'll it be today?

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: The good plate's out. You've more than earned a look at it.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: More ore for the walls? Bless you. Here, take this.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Since the siege I teach anyone who asks. Come, stand here.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Three strikes, each in the heart of the glow. That's all the secret there is.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Fire's banked and waiting. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How's the town doing?

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Busy. Loud. Full of merchants grumbling about the toll.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: It's wonderful. I haven't had a quiet hour in weeks.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: My steel comes from Ironhold, and they've gone quiet. Someone should check their mines.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Best ore I ever worked came out of the tundra. The men who found it didn't go back.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: If it doesn't sit right, bring it back. I'll fix it.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: Every strike makes you better. Come back anytime.

lines.speaker: oakArmorer
lines.text: You're always welcome here.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Looking or buying? Either's fine. Just don't touch the edges.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Senna. I sell blades. What you do with them is your business.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: So the siege broke. Good for the town. War was better for my trade, mind.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Back for something sharper?

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Sharp, balanced, and fairly priced. Take your time.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: I've sold to both sides of three wars. I'm still here. Most of them aren't.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Krag's men carry good steel. Syndicate money. Worth picking up, if you get the chance.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Quick blades want Dexterity. Bows and guns want Skill. Know which you are.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Keep it oiled. Rust ruins a good edge faster than bone.

lines.speaker: oakWeapons
lines.text: Try not to die owing me money.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: You didn't hear me come up behind you. Most people don't.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: They call me the Whisper. I teach people how not to be seen.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Town's quieter now. Fewer guards. Easier work, for some of us.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: The Syndicate counts you as a friend. Friends pay less. Remember that.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: The Syndicate wants you dead. I was paid to teach, not to kill. So, lessons.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: You're still too loud. We'll work on it.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Quietly, then. Watch my feet, not my hands.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Shadowblade?

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Someone who's already behind you. In, one cut, and gone.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Dexterity matters most. Skill, if you want the cut to count.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: You move well now. Take the rest. Bring some Skill for the smoke.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Your hands are quick enough. Next step.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Not yet. You're heavy on your feet. Work on your Dexterity.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Who are the Ashen Syndicate?

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: People who noticed the law has a price. I don't judge. I just get paid.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: Now practise where nobody can see you.

lines.speaker: trainerShadow
lines.text: You never saw me.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You may come closer. That's close enough.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Lord Castellan, of Oakhaven's oldest family. I teach command.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: My town stands, and my family's name with it. You have my thanks. Truly.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: A friend of the Order. I'll lower my fee. Please don't spread that around.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: The Order has your name on a list. I'll teach you anyway. Coin is coin.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Ah, you again. Shall we continue?

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Very well. Watch how an order is given, and how it's followed.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Grand Sovereign?

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Someone who doesn't fight alone. You call guards, and they fight for you.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: It takes Charisma. Nobody follows a leader they can't hear.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You have real presence now. Take the rest of my lessons.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Your voice carries. You're ready for the next lesson.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: I'm afraid no one would follow you yet. Work on your Charisma.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about your family.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: We built the walls Captain Hale stands on. He forgets that. I remind him.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Go on, then. Lead someone.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Good day to you.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Next! Oh, you're walking. That makes a nice change.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Brother Fenn. Forty wounded on the wall, and only one of me.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: No new wounded in three days. I barely know what to do with myself.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: You again, and on your own two feet. Good.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Lie down here, the clean cot. There. Flasks filled, off you go.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Mana draught. Tastes like old coins, but it works.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Can I carry more potions?

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: With a longer belt, yes. I sell those. Filling the flasks is free.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Krag's archers aim low. Keep moving and they'll mostly miss.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: I'm seeing burns, frostbite, and one man who swears a statue bit him.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Off you go. Next time, come for a chat instead of stitches.

lines.speaker: oakHealer
lines.text: Take care. And eat something.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: No names here. But I know who opened the gate. Everyone does.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: You can call me the Fence. Everything here came from somewhere.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: The Syndicate isn't fond of you right now. Your gold, though, is welcome.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: Back again. Nobody followed you, I hope?

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: No questions either way. The Syndicate takes its cut, you take the goods.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: Before the fire I sold candles. Honest work. It didn't pay.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Any armour for sale?

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: The armourers are gone, friend. You'd know why better than me.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: A fortress turned up in the far north last year. Nobody built it.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: Someone's buying every void crystal they can find. Not us. That worries me.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: You were never here.

lines.speaker: blackMarket
lines.text: Watch your step. The rubble shifts.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: A visitor. Please don't touch the jars.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Doctor Sangrel. Oakhaven's new owners don't ask what I teach. It's restful.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: You found me. Not many come looking for a doctor in a place like this.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Doctor Sangrel. Towns burn people like me, so I work where there aren't any.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: The Syndicate speaks for you. I charge its friends less. My standards stay the same.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: The Syndicate would pay well for your blood. I'd rather you spent it here.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: You look pale. Good. It suits the work.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Roll up your sleeve. It will hurt. That's rather the point.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Blood Alchemist?

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: You pay for power with your own health, then take it back from your enemies.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Endurance is what you have to spend. Intelligence is how well you spend it.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: A remarkable constitution. You may learn nearly all of it.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: You're sturdy enough for the next lesson.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: You'd faint at the first cut. Build your Endurance first, please.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What's in the jars?

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Samples. Freely given, for the most part.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Do keep notes. I'd like to hear how it goes.

lines.speaker: trainerBlood
lines.text: Stay healthy. I mean that.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: So you're the one who opened the gate. Sit down. You've earned a chair.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: They call me Madam Ash. Oakhaven is ours now. Partly thanks to you.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: The Dread Fortress, in our hands. You were worth every coin.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: You gave the throne to someone else. We'll talk about that. Not today.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: You've been working against us. Sit anyway. I like to know who I'm dealing with.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: Back again. What can the Syndicate do for you?

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I was promised a share of Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: And you'll have it. A share of a ruin, for now. Here's this season's.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: It'll grow. A ruin pays very well when you own its only market.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does the Syndicate actually want?

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: What everyone wants. We just don't pretend otherwise.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: Stay friendly, and the Whisper and the Doctor will charge you less.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: The Iron Order is after me.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: Of course they are. You burned one of their towns. Carry extra potions.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: The dwarves found something in their mines. A core. Bring it to us and name your price.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: The core arrived safely. You'd be amazed what it does to a lock.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: Everything worth having has moved north. So have we.

lines.speaker: syndicateBoss
lines.text: Don't be a stranger. We keep an eye on strangers.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: A newcomer. Do sit down, I don't bite. My prices do, a little.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: They call me Silky Ren. I collect fine things, one game at a time.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: Ah, my favourite opponent. Shall we?

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: The fee, please. Then lay something worth my while.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How do we play?

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: One item each, three times at most. The finer piece takes the point. Two points take the game.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: Your pieces stay with me either way. Win three games running and you'll leave with a real treasure.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: A dealer in rare things. I find them, I keep them, and now and then I lose one.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What do you do with it all?

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: I sort it by shine. The shiniest go on the top shelf, next to my teacups.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: Delightful. Do come back when your bag is heavier.

lines.speaker: oakGambler
lines.text: Mind your purse out there. Not everyone plays fair.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Free. Good. The cold did not take me, and neither did they.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Ivor Hask. Halvard Rimeheart taught me the frost. I teach it now, here.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: You return. Good.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Stand still. Let the cold come to you. Then send it back.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Frostwarden?

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Chill them, freeze them, then break the ice.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Strength for the blade. Intelligence for the frost.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: You are stronger than I was. Take what you need.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: You are ready. Next lesson.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Not yet. More strength of arm and of mind.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: I hunted in the tundra. They caged me for a winter.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Ironhold's forges are warm. I like it here.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Practise. The cold is patient. Be the same.

lines.speaker: frostDisciple
lines.text: Stay warm.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: You came up through the mines. I can smell the dust on you.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: Dorn. Forgemaster of Ironhold. And I've got a problem the size of a mountain.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: The light's out and the golems are scrap. My miners sang last night. First time in a year.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: Blue fire in my forges and robed scholars in my halls. The work is good, at least.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: You sold it. The golems still walk, and my mines are still a grave. Leave me be.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: So the throne's settled. Good. Maybe now we can get back to digging.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: What is it? The forge won't wait.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What happened down in the mines?

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: We dug for iron and found a heart. An aether core. You can feel it beating.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: And the golems?

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: They move to its rhythm. Three powers have written asking for it. I trust none of them.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: You'll reach it first, at the bottom of the Ironhold Mines. What happens then is up to you.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About the core...

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: You broke a wonder to save my people. The Order sent armourers. I sent ale.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: The Circle's people are odd, but their guns shoot straight. Fair enough.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: You did it for gold. I hope it keeps you warm.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about Ironhold.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: The best steel in the realm, when the mines are working.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: Stonefoot teaches earth, Pim teaches machines. Both will talk your ear off.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: East of the Crags the land turns white. Frostbite Tundra. Giants, and worse.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: My scouts saw a fortress up north that wasn't there last year. I don't like that.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: It all ends at the Dread Fortress. Every road north leads there.

lines.speaker: forgemaster
lines.text: Go well.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Careful with the display. Those are sharp on both edges.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Hilda Hammerhand. Every piece here was forged by dwarven hands.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: You killed the dragon? I hope it was with one of my blades.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Back for proper steel?

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Dwarf-forged. If one of these breaks, I'll want to know how.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Good, honest metal. Ironhold always pays for that.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: A surface-dweller at the anvil? Well, everyone starts somewhere.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: The glow tells you when. Your arm tells you how hard. Three strikes.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Mind the sparks, and don't touch my good hammer.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: My mother forged for kings. I forge for whoever comes through the door.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Those golems down there are made of our own iron. It stings, I'll tell you.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: A good blade does half the work. Your Strength has to do the rest.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Bring it back blunt and I'll know you've used it well.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: A dwarf would've done better. But not by much.

lines.speaker: ironWeapons
lines.text: Strike hard.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Careful, that one's loaded. Most of them are, actually.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Tinker Voss. The Circle sent me to study the core. It's taught us so much.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Ah, good. I've made a few changes since you were here.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Everything here came out of studying the core. Just don't point it at me.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What did the core teach you?

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: That metal can think, a little. I try not to dwell on that.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Guns run on Skill, and they run hot. Ask Pim about heat before you burn a hand.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Let me know how it handles. I'm keeping notes.

lines.speaker: ironAetherWorks
lines.text: Mind the recoil.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Garrun. Armour on the racks, rings in the tray.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Back. What do you need?

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: That plate will turn a giant's club. Have a look.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Let me weigh it. Good. The coin's yours.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Plate is patient work. I'll show you the basics.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Heat, strike, turn. Three strikes, right in the glow. Then let it cool.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: The forge is ready when you are.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: You don't say much, do you?

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Not much worth saying.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Giants in the tundra. Clubs like tree trunks. I'd take the heavy plate.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Demons up north. Fire and claws. I'd take the heavy plate.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Good choice.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Let it cool before you wear it.

lines.speaker: ironArmor
lines.text: Take care.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: You're the one who destroyed the core. The Order remembers that.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: I'm the Order's quartermaster here. Our armouries are open to you.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: The Order holds the Dread Fortress, thanks to you. At ease. You've earned it.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: The Order has you on a list. My orders say to sell to you anyway. I'll follow them.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: What do you need?

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Take what you need. The Order looks after its own.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: The Order buys all ore for the war. Your payment.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: The Order arms its friends. I will teach you.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Discipline at the anvil, as on the field. Three strikes, true to the glow.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Use the Order's forge with honour.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does the Order want from me?

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Nothing, for now. That doesn't happen often. Enjoy it.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: The Order will want the throne in the Dread Fortress. It'll remember who helped.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Look after it. It's Order property until you've bled in it.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Well forged. Serve well in it.

lines.speaker: ironOrderArmor
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Slow down. The mountain isn't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: They call me Old Stonefoot. I listen to the ground. Sometimes it answers.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: The mountain feels different since you went down there. Calmer, or emptier.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: A dragon flew over the peak yesterday and left us alone. Your doing, I'm told.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: There you are. I thought you'd be back.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Plant your feet. Feel that? No? That's where we start.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a Geomancer do?

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: We raise walls, call up spikes, and break the ground when we have to.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Strength to move the stone. Intelligence to know where it wants to go.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: The stone knows you now. Learn the rest when you're ready.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: You're steady enough for the next lesson.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Not yet. The stone won't move for you. Build your Strength.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Which faction do you serve?

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: None of them. Orders and guilds come and go. The mountain stays.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Take your time with it. The ground's patient.

lines.speaker: trainerGeo
lines.text: Walk softly.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Ah, wait, don't touch that! Or that. Stand on the rug, the rug's safe.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Gearwright Pim. I build guns, turrets, and a lot of heat gauges.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: You gave the core to the Circle! I've hardly slept since. In a good way.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: The Circle's angry about the oracle. I just build things. I'd rather not get involved.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: You're a friend of the Circle, so your lessons are cheaper. I did the paperwork.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: The Circle says I shouldn't teach you. I'm going to anyway. Don't tell them.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Oh good, you've still got all your fingers.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Right. Safety first, then the loud part.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is an Aether-Tech?

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Guns, turrets, and a heat gauge. Shoot, build, and vent before you lock up.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Mostly it's Skill. A bit of Intelligence for the bigger machines.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: You know your way around a turret now. Take the big machines.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Steady hands. You're ready for the next one.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Your aim's a bit shaky still. Put some points into Skill.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What happens if I overheat?

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Everything locks up for a few seconds. Vent early, vent often. Trust me on that.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: And remember to vent the heat before it vents you.

lines.speaker: trainerAether
lines.text: Be careful out there!

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Boots off at the door, please. I've only just swept.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Mother Brynja. I've set most of the broken bones in this mountain.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: You went to the Dread Fortress and came back. Sit down. Let me look at you.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Still alive. Good. Sit.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Drink this, and don't make that face. Your flasks are full.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Here. It tastes awful. Drink it when your magic runs out, not before.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Can I carry more potions?

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: I can sell you a longer belt. Five flasks is about all anyone can carry and still run.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: The tundra takes fingers and toes. Keep moving, and don't fall asleep in the snow.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: There's a drowned temple past the tundra. The naga there don't take prisoners.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Whatever's in that rift, I can't stitch it. Don't let it reach you.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Off you go. And eat something, you're too thin.

lines.speaker: ironHealer
lines.text: Come back in one piece.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You. You're the one who opened my gate.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: I teach in a cellar now, because I have to eat. Don't take it for forgiveness.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: So the throne's decided, and Oakhaven is still ashes. I hope it was worth it.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You're back. My fee hasn't changed.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: I'll teach you to command. Whether you deserve it is another matter.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Grand Sovereign?

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Someone others follow. Guards come when you call and fight at your word.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: It runs on Charisma. You have some. That's what makes it hard to forgive.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You have the presence for all of it. I wish you'd used it better.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: You're ready for the next lesson. I won't pretend I'm glad.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: No one would follow you yet. Work on your Charisma.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About Oakhaven...

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Three hundred years. My family built those walls.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Please don't explain. Nothing you could say would make it right.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Go. Practise on someone else.

lines.speaker: trainerSovereign
lines.text: Leave me, please.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: You killed her. I saw it coming for years, and it still hurts.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: I'm the Keeper of Hours. I'll teach you. She told me I would.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: There you are. I've been expecting you for a while. Or will have been.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: I'm the Keeper of Hours. I teach how to bend time, a little.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: She's free. For once I can't tell what happens next. It's wonderful.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: The Circle thinks well of you, so the lessons cost less. They decided that last week.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: The Circle's angry with you now. It passes. Until then, we'll keep this quiet.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: Welcome back. You're right on time.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: Watch closely. Then watch again, a moment earlier.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Chrono-Weaver?

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: We hold a foe still in time, hurry a friend along, and take back a mistake.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: Intelligence to see the thread. Skill to pull it.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: You hold the thread well. Take the rest whenever you like.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: You're ready. I could tell before you asked.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: The thread keeps slipping. More Intelligence, and more Skill.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about the oracle.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: She saw every ending except her own. Now she gets to find out.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: She didn't fight it. She'd seen it already. Please don't ask me again.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: She sees every ending. It's a heavy thing to carry. Be kind to her.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: It'll make sense later. It usually does.

lines.speaker: trainerChrono
lines.text: Until we meet again. Or before.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: I knew someone would come. The goblins never understood herbs. Or kindness.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: I'm Briar. I gather and dry what grows. Silverbridge was kind enough to take me in.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: Ah, hello again. Your boots smell of moss. Good.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: My stores were lost in that cage. Could you bring me three sunpetals?

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: They grow out on the plains. I'll pay well for them.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About those sunpetals...

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: Still looking? Sunpetals love the open sun.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Here are your sunpetals.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: Oh, these are perfect. Smell that!

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: Here, your payment. And my thanks, again.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: A herbalist from the hills. The goblins took me for a witch.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: They weren't entirely wrong.

lines.speaker: freedHerbalist
lines.text: Walk gently. Things grow there.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Mind the cart! Sorry, everything on this bridge moves. Welcome to Silverbridge.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: I'm Mayor Brenna Quill. If it's lost, broken or late, it ends up on my desk.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: The whole river's talking about you. Trade's never been better. So, thank you.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Back again? Good. Try not to block the carts.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Mayor, nine years now. Before that I sold rope. Same job, really. Holding things together.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: The town votes every spring. So far, nobody else wants the desk.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Tell me about Silverbridge.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: The bridge came first. Then a market on it, then houses, then houses on top of those.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Mind the fountains. Children fall in. So do grown-ups, on market day.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Is there really a teacher for every class here?

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Every single one. Shield, fire, shadow, stone. A master of each, all on one bridge.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Pupils come from all over. It's good for the inns. Less good for my windows.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What do people trade here?

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Whatever the river brings. Fish, silk, Ironhold steel, the odd crate of angry chickens.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: And not every trader in Silverbridge hangs out a sign. Keep your eyes open.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: The boats from the north have stopped. Something's burning up in the Ashen Crags.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: No Ironhold steel this month. The dwarves say something's gone wrong in their mines.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: The fur traders won't cross the tundra anymore. They say the giants are on the move.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Traders only whisper about the far north now. Whatever's up there, it isn't buying.

lines.speaker: mayorBrenna
lines.text: Off you go. And if anyone asks, the bridge toll is very fair.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Mm? Oh, a patient. Sorry, I was resting my eyes. Healers do that.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Friar Ansel. Come in, sit down. The chair's comfier than it looks.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Ah, you're back. And I'd only just sat down.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Lie back, close your eyes. Not for long, or I'll nod off too. There, flasks full.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Glowcap tonic. Good for the mind, bad for the breath. Sip it slowly.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Any advice on potions?

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Drink one before you're desperate. Heroes always wait too long.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: If you want to carry more, I sell longer belts. Filling the flasks is free.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you ever actually sleep?

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Not at night. Pupils from every class, all practising. Something always explodes.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Off you go. Next time, come for tea instead of bandages.

lines.speaker: sbHealer
lines.text: Mind the steps. Half my patients only tripped on them.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Oh! Mind the jars. That one bites. Well, it nibbles.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Odile Fernwhistle, alchemist. Bring me herbs and I'll bottle you a little courage.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: You're back! Did you bring me anything green?

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Could you brew me something?

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Let's see your pouch. Ooh, lovely. Pick what you want and I'll get the kettle on.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: I set my mum's garden on fire with a daisy. Nobody could explain it, so I had to learn.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Where do I find herbs?

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Out in the wild, everywhere you fight. Just walk over a plant and it's yours.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: The rare ones are choosy. Moonbells open in the Whispering Woods; shadowthorn wants the dark places.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What do the elixirs do?

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Each one makes you stronger in a fight for a whole minute. Harder hits, tougher skin, quicker feet.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: They sit in your third flask. Tap the little arrow to swap which one you drink.

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Careful with those, they're still warm. Come back when your pouch is full!

lines.speaker: sbAlchemist
lines.text: Bye now! If you see a purple flower, pick two. One for me.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Step right up! Twelve cards, one hourglass, and a purse that could double!

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Madame Pell. I never forget a face. Let's see if you never forget a card.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Back for another round? The sand's been waiting for you.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Coins on the cloth, eyes on the cards. Ready? Turn the glass!

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How does it work?

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Turn two cards. A pair stays up. Find every pair before the sand runs out and I pay double.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Win again and the glass gets quicker. Win five in a row and I'll hand you a legendary prize.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: I ran away with the travelling circus at nine. It turned out to be very good at maths.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Has anyone ever won the prize?

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: A dwarf, once. Nobody has seen him blink since.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Win or lose, that was a good game. Come back when your eyes are rested.

lines.speaker: sbGambler
lines.text: Off you go! Remember where you put your feet.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Shut the door, there's a draught. The moths are after my tapestries.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Alder Vane. Some call me the Collector. I buy rare things, and sell them to people I like.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: My friend! Come in, come in. I've dusted something special for you.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: You again. Still haven't done me that favour, I see.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: The cabinets are open. Only the best, and I remember every price.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you sell anything?

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Not to strangers. But do me a favour and we'll be friends.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Treants in the Whispering Woods guard the moonbells I need. Beat four of them and bring me two moonbells.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About that favour...

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Four treants, two moonbells. The moonbells won't pick themselves, sadly.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: I brought your moonbells.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Oh, they still smell of the woods! Wonderful.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: A deal's a deal. My cabinets are yours to look through, any time.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: I've collected since I was six. First it was buttons. Now it's swords that hum.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Treat that one kindly. It's older than both of us.

lines.speaker: sbCollector
lines.text: Close the door behind you. Gently, the vases rattle.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: You're staring. Either buy something or stop blocking my light.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Mirela Thorne. I find things people lose. Then I find them new owners.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Ah, my favourite hero. I kept the good stuff under the cloth for you.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Back? Remember what I asked. Then we can talk business.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Armour from all over. Don't ask where. It's all clean now, I promise.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What's under the cloth?

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Good armour. For friends. And friends do each other favours.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Bandits in the Oakhaven outskirts keep robbing my deliveries. Beat fifteen, then ask the trinket kid who sent them.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: About those bandits...

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Fifteen bandits, then a word with the trinket kid. Off you go.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: The bandits are beaten, and I know who sent them.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: So it was the gossip all along. Ha! I owe you one.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Lift the cloth whenever you like. Friends get first pick.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: I grew up on these river steps. Everything that floats past ends up with me sooner or later.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Wear it well. And if anyone asks, you bought it in Ironhold.

lines.speaker: sbFence
lines.text: Mind your purse. Not everyone here is as honest as me.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Ha! Look at that dent. I hope you got your money back for that armour.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Greta Ironvein. I make armour that comes home with its owner. Every time, so far.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: You again! Still in one piece. My favourite kind of customer.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Go on, knock on it. Hard as you like.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Lovely ore. Silverbridge always pays a fair price.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Want to try the hammer yourself? I don't mind sharing the forge.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Strike when it glows hottest. Three good strikes make a good piece.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Help yourself to the forge. Shout if anything catches fire.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Mountain family. I came downriver for the trade and stayed for the fish.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What makes good armour?

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: It's not how thick it is. It's where it bends. Good armour bends where you do.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Heavy plate wants Strength, mind. Wear it without and you'll waddle like a duck.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Wear it well. Bring me the dents, I like a good story.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Look at that! You're a natural.

lines.speaker: sbArmorer
lines.text: Off you go. Don't get hit anywhere I haven't covered.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Ah, a customer with taste. I can always tell. It's in the way you walk in.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Corvin Ashby, of Ashby's Fine Blades. Yes, that Ashby. You've heard of me, surely.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Back already? They always come back to Corvin.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Every blade polished by hand. My hand, in fact. Mind the reflection.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: The finest blade seller on the river. Ask anyone. Or just read my sign.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How do I pick a good weapon?

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Pick one that suits you. Quick hands want a light blade, strong arms a heavy one.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: And it should look good. Nobody runs from a hero with an ugly sword.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: A fine choice. Not quite as fine as my hair, but close.

lines.speaker: sbWeapons
lines.text: Do tell people where you bought it.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: Psst! Over here! Rings, charms, lucky stones. Best stall on the bridge.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: Name's Tam Marlow. I'm small, but my prices are smaller.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: My favourite customer! Don't tell the others I said that.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: All real. Mostly. Fine, that one's glass, but it's very nice glass.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: Grew up on this bridge. I know every crack, every cat and every shortcut.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Heard any good gossip?

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: Professor Sprocket blew his eyebrows off again. Third time this month.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: And the mayor knows about traders who don't hang out a sign. I'm working on it.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: Pleasure doing business! Tell your friends. Not the guards.

lines.speaker: sbJeweler
lines.text: See you around! I'll be right here. Probably.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Ha! Another young one. Chin up, shoulders back. Shields work better with a smile.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Dame Helga Stormshield. I held this bridge once. Now I teach others to hold their ground.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: There you are! Shield up? Good. Smiling? Even better.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Feet wide. Lean in. When I push, you don't move. Ready? Hup!

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does an Aegis Knight really do?

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: You stand in front, so the others don't have to. Best job there is.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Strength to lift the shield. Endurance to keep it up until supper.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: You're a proper wall now, dear. Take any lesson you like.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Steady legs! You're ready for the next one.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Not yet. One good push and you'd topple. More Strength and Endurance, please.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: You held this bridge?

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Forty years ago, against river pirates. Six of us, one gate, a very long night.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: We didn't win by hitting hardest. We won by not moving. Remember that.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Good work! Now eat something. Shields are heavy.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAegis
lines.text: Chin up out there!

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Do come in. Mind the notes, and please don't sneeze near the brazier.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Magister Ignatius Vale. I teach fire on a bridge. Plenty of water about, you see.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Punctual. Excellent. We'll begin where we stopped.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Observe. A small flame, held still. Big flames are easy. Small ones take skill.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a pyromancer really do?

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Anyone can start a fire. A pyromancer decides where it goes, and where it stops.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: It all comes from Intelligence. Later, Skill helps, when the fire needs a steady hand.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Your control is excellent. I've very little left to correct. Choose freely.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Adequate. More than adequate, actually. You may have the next lesson.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Not yet. Your flame wobbles. A sharper mind, please. More Intelligence.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What do you think of Professor Sprocket?

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Brilliant man. Loud, careless and brilliant. I keep a bucket by his door.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Practise near water. I insist.

lines.speaker: sbMasterPyro
lines.text: Good day. Do keep your sleeves rolled up.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Looking for me? I've been next to you since the fountain. You walked past me twice.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Nyx Halloway. The best place to hide is a crowd, and this is the busiest bridge there is.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Hi again. I've been here a while. You noticed? No? Good.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Lesson one: walk like you belong. Nobody looks twice at someone who belongs.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What makes a good Shadowblade?

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Never being where they're looking. Slip in, one quick strike, and blend back in.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Dexterity for quick feet and hands. Skill, so the strike counts.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: You're properly sneaky now. Take what's left, you've earned it.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Light on your feet! You're ready for the next trick.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Not yet. I can hear you coming from the fountain. More Dexterity.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How did you learn all this?

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: I used to pick pockets on this very bridge. I was good at it, too.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Then the mayor caught me and gave me a job, not a cell. Don't tell her I'm grateful.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: Now go and practise. Try not to let me catch you.

lines.speaker: sbMasterShadow
lines.text: See you. Well, you won't see me.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Oh! Hello, hello. Do forgive me, I was chatting with my guards. Lovely listeners.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Percival Ashcombe. I could teach in a castle, but you only learn to lead where people are.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: My dear friend! Shall we carry on? Only if you'd like to, of course.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Right then. A good order is clear, kind, and only given once. Like so.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Grand Sovereign?

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: A leader. Your guards come to your side and fight with you, not just for you.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Charisma is everything. People follow those they like. And who remember their names.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Splendid! People would follow you anywhere now. Take all the lessons.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Your guards would listen to you. You're ready for the next lesson.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Not quite yet, I'm afraid. A little more Charisma, and they'll come.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Do you really say please to your guards?

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Always. Shouting gets you obeyed. Please gets you loyalty, and loyalty lasts longer.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Lovely work. Remember to thank them afterwards.

lines.speaker: sbMasterSovereign
lines.text: Do take care, and give my regards to everyone.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Mind the moss, dear, it's had a long week. Now, let's have a look at you.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Grandmother Tova Deeproot. The river bed here is lovely stone, all the way down.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Back already? Sit, I've just made tea. Stone tea. It's mostly tea.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Hands flat on the ground. Not like that. Like you're patting a sleepy dog.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does a Geomancer do?

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: We ask the ground for help. A wall when you need one, a spike when someone's rude.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Stone's like a garden. Strength to dig, Intelligence to know where to plant.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: The ground likes you now. Learn whatever you please, dear.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Good roots! You're ready for the next lesson.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Not yet, love. The stone won't budge for you. More Strength first.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Is that a garden made of stone?

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Forty years of work. Every rock grown by hand. Well, by magic. Mostly by hand.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Take a pebble on your way out. They make lovely doorstops.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Lovely. Now go and dig something. Gently.

lines.speaker: sbMasterGeo
lines.text: Off you go. Wrap up warm, it's damp by the river.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Welcome, welcome! You're just in time for the demonstration. Cover your ears, please.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Professor Quint Sprocket. The river turns my wheels for free. Where else would I teach?

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Ah, my favourite pupil! Today's demonstration is extra loud.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Observe the blackboard. Now forget the blackboard, and watch the machine.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What does an Aether-Tech actually do?

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: We build our way out of trouble. A pistol, a turret, and a heat gauge to keep you honest.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Skill for the aim, Intelligence for the clever bits. Ideally both.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Marvellous! You could give my lectures. Please don't, though. Take the rest.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: A steady hand! You're ready for the next machine.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Not yet. Your aim drifts. More Skill, then we'll talk.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What happened to your eyebrows?

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: A demonstration went slightly too well. They'll grow back. They always do.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Splendid. Now go and vent that heat. Outside, ideally.

lines.speaker: sbMasterAether
lines.text: Class dismissed! Do mind the steps.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: My old pupil, the Keeper of Hours, wrote that you'd come. At this very minute, in fact.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Clockwarden Selwyn. I keep the bridge clock. A town this busy can't afford to be late.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Seven minutes after the hour. A good time to begin.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Count with me. One, two, and hold. Time stretches, if you hold it right.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Chrono-Weaver?

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: We tidy up time. Slow a foe down, hurry a friend along, undo the odd mistake.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Intelligence to understand it. Skill to touch it without breaking anything.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Excellent timing. Take the rest of my lessons whenever it suits you.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: You're ready. The next lesson starts, oh, now.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Not yet. You're always a beat behind. More Intelligence, and more Skill.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: How do you know the Keeper of Hours?

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: I taught him, years ago. A brilliant pupil. Always early or late, never on time.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Practise every day. Same time each day, if you please.

lines.speaker: sbMasterChrono
lines.text: Off you go. Don't be late.

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
lines.text: Doctor Sangrel wrote to me about you. He says you didn't faint. High praise, from him.

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
lines.text: Vesper Crimsonleaf. Every herb in the world floats past this bridge. I'm spoiled here.

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
lines.text: Welcome back. You look lively today. I can always tell.

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
lines.text: Breathe in. Feel your strength? Now spend a little of it. Wisely.

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: What is a Blood Alchemist, really?

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
lines.text: We spend our own life force for power, then take it back from our foes.

lines.speaker: sbMasterBlood
